subject: Intermittent token stream disconnects & elevated error-rate — Calypso Payments
messages:
From: Elliot Sharp <elliot.sharp@calypso-payments.com>
To: support@redwood-inference.com
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 09:12:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Production errors with streaming tokens / disconnects

Hey team,

We started seeing an uptick in token-level errors and client disconnects on our integration around 08:45 PDT. Error rate jumped from ~0.4% to ~6% and a couple of our flows experienced severe latency spikes (p99 from 320ms to ~2.3s). The failures correlate with high throughput (large batched requests) and appear during streaming responses — clients report partial JSON fragments and abrupt connection resets.

We're on your JS client SDK v2.3.1, running behind a proxy that does some light header inspection. Attached are logs (truncated) and a packet capture around the most recent incident. Happy to hop in a call — this is impacting a key payout path.

Elliot
Platform Ops — Calypso Payments
ops@calypso-payments.com

From: rishi_malhotra <rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com>
To: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>, marissa_cole <marissa_cole@redwood-inference.com>, markus_klein <markus_klein@redwood-inference.com>
Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 10:15:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors with streaming tokens / disconnects — initial triage

Triage notes (quick):
- Reproduced locally with SDK v2.3.1 behind a header-inspecting proxy. The SDK streaming parser expects header frames and token chunks delimited in a single buffer; our tests show the proxy sometimes splits the CRLF boundaries across TCP segments.
- The SDK’s parser does a naive indexOf('

') search and then slices; when the boundary is split, the parser treats leading bytes of the next chunk as continuation of a header line, producing malformed header maps and a subsequent mismatch in content-length / chunked framing validation. This can lead to dropped frames, token duplication in KV cache, and long tail latency from repeated retries.
- Server-side logs show elevated 5xxs (502/504) at the same timestamps; the runtime is returning partial responses while client retries cause transient spikes.

Immediate mitigations we can deploy:
1) Revert clients to SDK v2.2.8 (previously stable) — we can provide an automated npm flag and a short advisory.
2) Push a hotfix to SDK v2.3.x that performs streaming-safe boundary assembly (buffer until boundary or max-safe-wait) — estimate 6–8 hours to ship Canary and verify.
3) Server-side: enable more tolerant chunk-acceptor mode for Calypso (can be toggled per-tenant) to accept split-boundary frames for 24 hours while clients rotate.

I recommend combination (1) + (3) immediately to reduce customer pain, while we finish (2) for a permanent fix.

I’ll open an internal GitHub issue with repro steps and the packet capture attached.

Rishi
Principal Software Engineer, Inference Runtime
rishi_malhotra@redwood-inference.com

Attachments: packet-capture-0818.txt

From: hannah_schmitt <hannah_schmitt@redwood-inference.com>
To: Elliot Sharp <elliot.sharp@calypso-payments.com>

Date: Tue, 18 Aug 2026 12:02:00 -07:00
Subject: Re: Production errors with streaming tokens / disconnects — action and exec escalation

Elliot — quick update and proposed path: thanks for the packet captures.

What we’re doing now (live):
- Temporary tenant toggle: enabling tolerant chunk-acceptor for Calypso (takes effect in ~5 mins). This should immediately reduce decoding errors and cut the error rate by ~80% based on the repro.
- Workaround for customers: switching to SDK v2.2.8 if you can cut a release this afternoon. We’ll provide an npm rollback command and a short compatibility note.
- Engineering is building a proper parser fix (Rishi — ETA ~6–8 hrs) and we’ll canary to 5% of traffic before broad rollout.

Marissa / Markus — flagging this for exec attention: the customer is a strategic mid-market account with volume-sensitive flows. If tolerant-mode reduces errors but recovery is slow, they are likely to request credits. Please advise on pre-approved goodwill credit (we should be aligned to reduce churn).

Elliot — can you confirm whether your proxy can accept a temporary header bypass or whether you prefer the SDK rollback? If you can accept the tolerant-mode toggle, we’ll hold off the rollback and prioritize the SDK fix.

Regards,
Hannah
Sr. Customer Success Manager | Redwood Inference
